documents.title: USF Guidance for Ethical Generative AI Usage
documents.stance_why: The document sets no rule of its own for coursework: "use of genAI tools within university coursework is at the discretion of the instructor and students are expected to follow course-specific policies." The rest is general principles for all users, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: The Provost's Oct 2023 guidance sets seven principles for ethical genAI use (human-centered, responsibility, bias, sourcing, transparency, discipline-specific, data protection). It leaves coursework use to the instructor and tells students to follow course policies.

notes: Reconciled from coder A (118 units) and coder B (130 units). Only university-layer documents exist (school and computing none-found; course layer deferred). The genai.usf.edu university-guidance page repeats the 2023 Provost principles PDF with updates (Copilot replaces Bing Chat Enterprise; adds workforce-readiness and public-chatbot sections), so overlapping units are coded in both documents. The PDF text has ligature corruption (e.g. 'expectaIons'); some anchors reproduce it. Coder A noted that the acceptable-use sample lists 'examinations' among permitted submissions although its own example bars AI on unit exams; this is kept in the fit note of the permission unit. Neither coder proposed new types. One unit was set to UNCOVERED at reconciliation (ban template's 'limited exceptions' for accessibility accommodations or instructor-provided tools), and three more stay UNCOVERED or were coded as such by one coder (transparency-builds-trust rationale, 'students must responsibly use these tools'). No unit was dropped.
